cases.name: Mary Danner
cases.narrative: On July 25, 2018, her mother, Mary Danner, got into an argument with her live-in boyfriend about moving back to Pennsylvania. Danner had been diagnosed with inoperable kidney cancer, and as she faced the end of her life, she realized she wanted to be close to her family in York County, Penn. The argument over whether to move to Pennsylvania escalated. Sandridge shoved her, according to court records. Danner threatened to report him to his probation officer. Danner cut off the argument, saying she was going to lie down on the couch for a while. Sandridge walked to the bedroom and got one of his oxygen tanks, and when he returned to the living room, struck Danner in the head with it. He later told a detective that he reasoned that if Danner would turn him in for shoving her, she certainly would turn him in for hitting her on the head with the oxygen tank. So he struck her three more times with such force that when her body was found a few days later, blood covered the bottom half of the tank and had spattered onto photographs hanging in the wall above the couch. He told the detective that he watched for a few minutes as Danner drew her last breaths.

cases.name: Loretta Gail Jones
cases.about: Her obituary said, "She was a loving and devoted mom, mammy, and sister. Her family was her whole world, and her grandchildren were her pride and joy. She will be deeply missed by everyone who knew her."
